_comment: The REWORK Proof MCP server's tools and the fixed sentences it returns, in one file. Two servers read it: this package (stdio, index.js beside this file) and the hosted server REWORK runs at https://api.reworkdigital.io/mcp, so neither can describe a tool, or the ceiling on a claim, differently from the other. Every tool only reads: readOnlyHint is true on all of them.

server.name: rework-proof
server.title: REWORK Proof
server.description: Check whether delivered work is genuinely the author's: verify a REWORK credential, see whether it was revoked or ever issued, and read what it does and does not prove.
server.instructions: Read `assurance_note` with every result: it states the ceiling on what the result proves. A valid signature is not a review of the work.

protocols._comment: Revisions of the Model Context Protocol this server speaks, newest first. `handshake` revisions begin with `initialize`. `stateless` revisions have no handshake: every request names its revision in `params._meta`.

tools.name: verify_rework_credential
tools.title: Verify a REWORK credential
tools.description: Check whether a REWORK Verifiable Credential (a VC-JWT) is authentic, and report what it claims. Use this when someone presents a credential as evidence that they produced a piece of work. Returns whether the signature is valid, whether REWORK has since revoked it, who issued it, and the credential subject.

credential.description: The compact VC-JWT, three base64url segments separated by dots.

valid.description: True only when the signature verifies against REWORK's key, the credential has not expired, and REWORK has not revoked it.

reason.description: Why the credential is not valid; null when it is.

revoked.description: True when REWORK revoked the credential after issuing it; false when it was checked and stands; null when there is nothing to check (not a certificate credential, or not valid) or the status could not be read.

issuer.description: Who issued the credential, as the credential states it; null when it is not valid.

credential_subject.description: What the credential claims. Empty when it is not valid.

assurance_note.description: The ceiling on what this result proves. Read it before relying on the result.

tools.name: get_rework_issuer_keys
tools.title: Get REWORK's public signing keys
tools.description: Fetch REWORK's public signing keys (JWKS). Use this to verify a credential offline yourself instead of trusting this server, or to confirm the issuer key a credential names actually belongs to REWORK.

keys.description: REWORK's public signing keys, as a JSON Web Key Set.

tools.name: explain_rework_assurance
tools.title: Explain a REWORK assurance level
tools.description: Explain what a REWORK assurance level or credential type proves, and what it explicitly does not prove. Use this before relying on a credential, so a weak claim is not read as a strong one.

assurance.description: Assurance level, e.g. "workflow-identity". Omit to list all.

outputSchema.description: One level when `assurance` was given, every level otherwise, or `error` with the known levels when the level asked for does not exist.

tools.name: lookup_rework_attestation
tools.title: Look up whether REWORK issued a credential
tools.description: Check whether REWORK actually ISSUED a credential - not just whether its signature verifies. A forged-but-well-formed token fails this; a real one returns its issuance record and the CURRENT OpenTimestamps receipt, which may have been upgraded to a Bitcoin confirmation since issue. Pass the credential (its sha256 is the lookup key) or the digest directly.

credential.description: The VC-JWT. Only its sha256 digest is used as the lookup key; the credential itself is not stored.

digest.description: sha256 hex of the credential, if you already have it.

issued.description: Whether REWORK has a record of issuing a credential with this digest.

assurance_note.description: The ceiling on what this result proves. Read it before relying on the result.

annotations.title: Look up whether REWORK issued a credential

credential_types.REWORKWorkflowAttestation: A CI run whose repository identity GitHub attested via OIDC.
credential_types.REWORKHfJoinedPublication: A Hugging Face publication joined to the CI run that preceded it, confirmed by REWORK's own read of the Hub.
credential_types.REWORKProofOfWorkCredential: A submitted piece of work that passed REWORK verification.
credential_types.REWORKVideoProvenanceReceipt: A reviewed demonstration video, fingerprinted against reuse.
credential_types.REWORKReputationPassport: A holder's full verified history in one signed credential.
credential_types.REWORKReputationSummary: A summary of already-public verified facts about a holder.

ai_declaration.reads: Commit messages only: a Co-authored-by, Assisted-by or Generated-by trailer naming one of the tools below; an Assisted-by trailer in the AGENT:MODEL form; a Claude-Session, Amp-Thread-ID or Replit-Commit-Author trailer; an `AI-assisted: true` line; or a "Generated with" line.
ai_declaration.zero_means: No commit message declared a tool. It does not mean no tool was used; a message with no trailer looks the same either way.
ai_declaration.declared_means: The author chose to say so. It is reported as a fact and never lowers a result.

notes.unknown_assurance: Assurance level not recognised - do not assume this proves more than it states.
notes.issued: Issuance confirms REWORK signed a credential with this digest. It is still not a review of the code or a claim the work is any good - and a "submitted" timestamp is a calendar promise, only "confirmed" means anchored in Bitcoin.
notes.not_issued: REWORK has no record of issuing a credential with this digest. A valid signature with no issuance record deserves suspicion: it could predate the registry, or it could be a key compromise.
notes.revoked: REWORK revoked this credential after issuing it. Its signature still verifies, which is exactly why revocation has to be checked: do not rely on it.
notes.revocation_unchecked: Whether this credential has since been revoked could not be checked just now. The signature is valid; treat the result as incomplete.

errors.credential_required: credential is required: pass the compact VC-JWT (three base64url segments separated by dots)
errors.digest_required: pass either `credential` (the VC-JWT) or `digest` (64 hex chars)
